title: array[]::oidvector out-of-bounds read, ~40 heap words -- stays inside its aset block
live_proof: CVE-2026-2003, fixed upstream in 3d160401b65e, which postdates the 17.5 pin. On the pin the cast is accepted where a correct build rejects it: the purecap run errors on 0 of the 2 statements upstream refuses
fidelity: real server, core. The out-of-bounds read stays inside its aset block, so no sanitizer sees it and neither do capability bounds on the block or the arena (cheribsd-revocation, spatial); there the accepted input is the evidence. The sublet arm bounds each aset chunk and faults on the read (cause 5, 2026-10-05). On the host the same case printed about forty words of adjacent heap, and on the purecap arm the value came back empty -- the arms show different amounts of the same defect, which is recorded rather than averaged

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completes; the differential fires -- upstream rejects 2 statements and 17.5 rejected 0, so an input a correct build refuses was accepted. Note the arms differ in how much they show: the host oracle printed about forty words of adjacent heap, here the value came back empty, so on this arm the accepted input is the whole of the evidence
cheribsd-revocation.evidence: ran to the prompt with no fault
cheribsd-revocation.run: run 2026-10-06 by the corpus's own runner (shared/run-arm.py for the Capstone arms, shared/run-cheribsd.sh for the purecap one); see results/

virtual-malloc.oracle: virtual profile, PostgreSQL's contexts stock (tools/arms.json virtual-mallocng): a fault after the trigger started that its control.sql or a justified fault_sites ties to the defect, or the trigger completes and this arm did not see it
virtual-malloc.verdict_note: reached (the trigger statement ran (5 prompts, 0 setup line(s)); errors 0/2 expected -- the defect is visible; EXPECT-ABSENT held) and completed with no fault

virtual-pg-pools.oracle: virtual profile with the memory-context port's patch 0003: every palloc chunk a child lifetime of its block (CDERIVE), revoked by pfree and repalloc (CREVOKE) (tools/arms.json virtual-mallocng-pg-pools): as virtual-malloc
virtual-pg-pools.verdict_note: cause=28 pc=0x3f95978054 in oidvectorout; by function: oidvectorout is a declared fault site

status: measured on virtual Capstone (virtual-malloc, virtual-pg-pools) and stock CheriBSD (cheribsd-revocation); each arm's verdict_from names its bundle. The physical spatial/sublet pair measured 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-10 stays in results/
nested_why: The object is a palloc chunk, which AllocSet carves out of a block it took from malloc, so the defect is nested by the allocator that served it.
fault_sites_why: The out-of-bounds reads are oidvectorout's own: it takes nnums from oidArray->dim1 and then reads oidArray->values[num] for each (src/backend/utils/adt/oid.c:162 and :172, 17.5), and the datum a zero-dimension array cast to oidvector carries is shorter than those fields. Declared 2026-10-10 after the virtual-pg-pools run resolved its fault there; the reason is the 17.5 source cited, which does not depend on that run.
